items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Elmon Chambers couldn't find his mouth... And so, we sounded so terrible that Dodson came out on the stage... We went on and did very fine for that show.

ctx.x: Y-o-n-d-e-r. Wait a minute, what was his name? I can't think of his name now. But, this dancer was as good as Bill Robinson. But he made one mistake. He went into -- he left for Waterville to go for the burlesque. And burlesque is a step below vaudeville.. See, instead of going up. So, anyhow, Dancing Dodson was his name. Dancing Dodson. Well, Dodson came to us and here was another experience that we had

that was very good, because he was working at the Regent Theater. And he heard about the band, so we had a nice little band there, so he come down one day to listen to the band and he was talking to Bricktop and a couple of other entertainers there. So he said, "How would you boys like to come on and try to -- have you ever been on stage?" We said "no we hadn't". So he said, "Well, I'll tell you what I'm going to do. I'm going to give you a chance. I'm going to bring you down there and let you do a couple of…

And so, we sounded so terrible that Dodson came out on the stage and said, "Wait a minute, that's enough of this foolishness." He said, "Let me straighten you guys out. After all, you're here to play some good music for the people, not to clown and kid like you would in the cabaret." You know? But that settled us. We went on and did very fine for that show. And he kept us there for two or three days, you know. Because it wasn't paid. But that was our first chance.
